record.where: v3.13 — LIGHT BEHAVES (a retraction, then the fix)

clauses.text: Everything dark is now a layer: the night palette, and the quiet's grey dim (the day field was split — its warm bands are paint, drawn straight to the ground and never touched; its dim bands joined the darkness layer)

Every local light — the walker's lantern, a generator, a watchtower, a camp fire, the peddler's cart, a lumen bloom, a companion in the dark — erases banded holes in that layer on the terrain's own texel grid: a solid heart, two hems of ordered dither, nothing else

figure.note: the heart gone, a mid hem half gone, an outer hem mostly intact, the night whole past them

clauses.text: What shows through a hole is the ground's real colours
no partial alpha anywhere — a texel of night is either gone or intact, and falloff is carried entirely by dither coverage
The old glow discs are dead; emitters keep a bloom a few texels wide at the flame itself, nothing on the ground
ground inside the lantern pool is ×7.3 the brightness of the same meadow 260 u away

figure.note: at least ×4 on the suite's own unlit meadow at full night (measured ×5.32 there; the record's ×7.3 was its own meadow's)

clauses.text: reads as green-led terrain with zero painted-gold pixels

figure.note: not one warm, bright pixel on the ground in the lamp's reach

clauses.text: the falloff steps 0.05 → 0.60 → 1.00 through the hems

figure.note: the heart at most 0.05 intact, the mid hem 0.35–0.65, the outer hem 0.65–0.9, the night beyond at least 0.99, rising in that order

clauses.text: A generator carves the same pool at its camp
by day the lantern clears the grey dim off the ground the walker holds
on station-lit ground there is nothing to punch

checks.title: THROUGH THE HOLE, THE GROUND ITSELF
THE TEXEL GRID IS THE WORLD'S
BY DAY THE LANTERN CLEARS THE GREY DIM
ON STATION-LIT GROUND THERE IS NOTHING TO PUNCH
